description: Reason about time and space growth and use that model to improve data-intensive application code.

archetypes.name: Complexity-Aware Record Matching
archetypes.coreConcept: Estimate how work grows with input size, then trade additional memory for fewer repeated searches when matching records by a stable key.
mentalModel: Count how many times each input element is visited as the input grows.
A nested scan can compare each record against many records, producing quadratic growth.
Building a keyed index costs additional linear memory and setup work, then supports repeated constant-time average lookups.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Each record is indexed once and each matching record is emitted once in source order, with unmatched records excluded.

cognitiveTraps.name: Repeated Nested Search
cognitiveTraps.description: Keeping a full scan inside another full scan makes matching work grow roughly with the product of both collection sizes.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: For two collections with n records each, compare each left record against every right record; the number of comparisons grows near n squared.

cognitiveTraps.name: Ignoring the Index Memory Cost
cognitiveTraps.description: Claiming a faster lookup is free while omitting the auxiliary storage required to build the index.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Describe a keyed lookup as constant extra space even though a map retains one entry for each indexed record.

realWorldDomains.description: Matching shipment events to manifest entries using a shipment identifier while preserving event order.

qualityChecks.check: Repeated record matching reuses an index built from the lookup collection instead of rescanning that full collection for every input record.
qualityChecks.why: Reusing the index changes repeated matching work from quadratic growth to linear expected work while making the memory tradeoff explicit.

qualityChecks.check: Complexity explanations identify which input sizes drive the work and include auxiliary storage when an index is retained.
qualityChecks.why: A complexity label without its input dimensions or memory cost can hide the real scaling limit and tradeoff.

archetypes.name: Recursive Base-Case and Progress Trace
archetypes.coreConcept: A recursive function terminates when every reachable path reaches a base case, and each recursive step moves its input toward that case.
mentalModel: Write down the input for the current call before following its recursive call.
A base case returns without creating another frame.
A recursive case must make measurable progress toward a base case.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every reachable recursive path decreases the remaining problem measure until a base case returns.

cognitiveTraps.name: Base Case Boundary Shift
cognitiveTraps.description: Stopping one call too early or too late changes the result or causes an extra recursive call.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A countdown intended to include zero returns at one, or recurses from zero to a negative value.

cognitiveTraps.name: No Progress Toward the Base Case
cognitiveTraps.description: A recursive call preserves or increases the measure needed to reach termination.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A recursive countdown calls itself with the same count when count is positive.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing a bounded retry policy whose remaining-attempt count moves toward a stopping case.

qualityChecks.check: Each recursive path changes the relevant input measure toward a reachable base case.
qualityChecks.why: A call that does not make progress can recurse indefinitely or exceed the runtime stack.

qualityChecks.check: Base cases match the function's stated boundary contract and return without another recursive call.
qualityChecks.why: An off-by-one base case changes boundary behavior and may add an unnecessary frame.

archetypes.name: Call-Stack Frames and Return Unwinding
archetypes.coreConcept: Each recursive invocation has its own parameters and suspended return point; values combine or pass back as calls unwind.
mentalModel: Record each invocation as a distinct frame with its own argument values.
The deepest frame that reaches a base case returns first.
Resume suspended expressions from the deepest caller outward.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A caller resumes exactly once after its child returns, using that child's returned value in the suspended expression.

cognitiveTraps.name: Unwind Order Reversed
cognitiveTraps.description: Applying caller operations before the deepest call has returned.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: For total(n) = n + total(n - 1), add from the outermost frame downward instead of returning from the base case upward.

cognitiveTraps.name: Recursive Frames Treated as Shared State
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming each invocation overwrites the prior invocation's parameter or local value.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Treating local index values from nested calls as one mutable index rather than separate frame bindings.

cognitiveTraps.name: Sibling Calls Reuse a Prior Frame's State
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming a later independent recursive call begins with a local value left by an earlier sibling call.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A route-depth audit starts both region walks at depth zero, but a trace carries the first region's final depth into the second region.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing recursive subtotal aggregation across nested invoice groups.

qualityChecks.check: Values belonging to separate recursive invocations remain distinguishable while tracing the call stack.
qualityChecks.why: Each invocation owns its own parameter and local bindings until its frame returns.

qualityChecks.check: Post-call work is evaluated only after the child invocation returns, in last-in-first-out order.
qualityChecks.why: The call stack suspends each caller until the nested call supplies its return value.

archetypes.name: Nested Structure Recursion Trace
archetypes.coreConcept: Recursive rules can decompose a nested structure into smaller child problems, with each leaf or empty structure providing a stopping condition.
mentalModel: At each frame, identify the current node and the children that create new calls.
Trace sibling calls in source order while keeping each branch's return separate.
Combine a node's local contribution with the results returned by its children.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every recursive child is a strict substructure, and each node contributes exactly once to the final result.

cognitiveTraps.name: Empty Structure Lacks a Base Case
cognitiveTraps.description: The recursive rule attempts to inspect children when the current structure is empty.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A nested list traversal reads the first element without handling an empty list.

cognitiveTraps.name: A Branch Result Is Omitted
cognitiveTraps.description: One child result is not included when a recursive rule combines sibling branches.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A folder-size calculation visits subfolders but returns only the current folder's direct files.

realWorldDomains.description: Following recursive directory-size or quota calculations over nested folders.

qualityChecks.check: Each recursive child call receives a strictly smaller part of the current structure.
qualityChecks.why: Strictly smaller subproblems make structural progress toward an empty or leaf base case.

qualityChecks.check: The trace accounts for the local contribution and every required child result exactly once.
qualityChecks.why: Missing or duplicated branch results produce incorrect aggregates on nested data.
